papers.title: Cell Encapsulation and 3D Bioprinting for Therapeutic Cell Transplantation.
papers.abstract: The promise of cell therapy has been augmented by introducing biomaterials, where intricate scaffold shapes are fabricated to accommodate the cells within. In this review, we first discuss cell encapsulation and the promising potential of biomaterials to overcome challenges associated with cell therapy, particularly cellular function and longevity. More specifically, cell therapies in the context of autoimmune disorders, neurodegenerative diseases, and cancer are reviewed from the perspectives of preclinical findings as well as available clinical data. Next, techniques to fabricate cell-biomaterials constructs, focusing on emerging 3D bioprinting technologies, will be reviewed. 3D bioprinting is an advancing field that enables fabricating complex, interconnected, and consistent cell-based constructs capable of scaling up highly reproducible cell-biomaterials platforms with high precision. It is expected that 3D bioprinting devices will expand and become more precise, scalable, and appropriate for clinical manufacturing. Rather than one printer fits all, seeing more application-specific printer types, such as a bioprinter for bone tissue fabrication, which would be different from a bioprinter for skin tissue fabrication, is anticipated in the future.

summary_zh.motivation: 综述生物材料与3D生物打印在细胞治疗中的应用进展

summary_en.motivation: This review summarizes the potential of biomaterials and 3D bioprinting to overcome challenges in cell therapy, particularly for autoimmune disorders, neurodegenerative diseases, and cancer.
summary_en.method: The authors discuss cell encapsulation, biomaterial strategies, and emerging 3D bioprinting technologies for fabricating cell-biomaterial constructs.
summary_en.result: The review anticipates that future 3D bioprinters will become more application-specific, precise, and scalable for clinical manufacturing.
summary_en.validation: No experimental validation; the paper is a literature review synthesizing preclinical and clinical findings.

papers.title: Study on the Tensile and Shear Behaviors of Selective Laser Melting Manufactured Ti6Al4V
papers.first_author_affiliation: School of Mechanical Engineering, Yangzhou University, Yangzhou, 225127, China

corresponding_authors.name: Hao Zhang
corresponding_authors.affiliation: School of Mechanical Engineering, Yangzhou University, Yangzhou, 225127, China

llm.relevance_to_user: 论文研究了SLM制造Ti6Al4V的拉伸和剪切力学性能，为生物医学植入物提供基础材料数据，但未涉及多孔结构或应力遮挡。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address porous structures, stress shielding, fatigue behavior, or surface roughness relevant to biomedical implant design.

summary_zh.motivation: 表征选区激光熔化Ti6Al4V的拉伸和剪切性能
summary_zh.method: 通过SLM制备试样并进行拉伸和剪切力学测试
summary_zh.result: 获得了材料的强度、延展性等力学性能数据

summary_en.motivation: To characterize the tensile and shear mechanical properties of SLM-manufactured Ti6Al4V for potential biomedical applications.
summary_en.method: Specimens were fabricated by selective laser melting and subjected to tensile and shear tests to obtain mechanical response.
summary_en.result: Mechanical properties including ultimate strength, yield strength, and ductility were quantified.
summary_en.validation: Experimental mechanical testing provided direct validation of the material behavior.

summary_en.motivation: To fabricate localized diamond-filled copper structures for improved thermal management.
summary_en.method: Combined selective laser melting and spark plasma sintering to produce the composite.
summary_en.result: Dense diamond-copper composite structures were successfully fabricated.
summary_en.validation: Validation through microstructure characterization and thermal conductivity measurements.

llm.relevance_to_user: 本文仅关注全髋关节置换术的失血量，未涉及任何生物力学分析或植入物设计。
llm.why_not_core: No biomechanical modeling, no stress shielding or micromotion quantification, no finite element analysis, and no contact mechanics.

summary_zh.motivation: 比较骨水泥型和混合型全髋关节置换术的失血量差异
summary_zh.method: 回顾性分析临床数据，比较两种固定方式的失血量
summary_zh.result: 骨水泥型和混合型全髋关节置换术失血量更低

summary_en.motivation: To compare blood loss between cemented and hybrid total hip arthroplasty techniques.
summary_en.method: Retrospective analysis of clinical data from patients undergoing primary THA with either cemented or hybrid fixation.
summary_en.result: Cemented and hybrid THA resulted in lower blood loss compared to other fixation methods.
summary_en.validation: Clinical retrospective study with patient records and statistical analysis.

papers.title: Can Selected Use of Cemented and Uncemented Femoral Components in a Broad Population Produce Comparable Results Following Primary Total Hip Arthroplasty for Osteoarthritis?
papers.first_author_affiliation: Department of Orthopedic Surgery, Mayo Clinic, Rochester, Minnesota

corresponding_authors.name: Rafael J. Sierra
corresponding_authors.affiliation: Department of Orthopedic Surgery, Mayo Clinic, Rochester, Minnesota

llm.relevance_to_user: 临床对比研究，未涉及有限元分析或应力遮挡等力学问题，与用户方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not perform any finite element analysis, stress shielding quantification, or micromotion modeling; it is a clinical outcomes study without biomechanical evaluation.

summary_zh.motivation: 比较骨水泥与非骨水泥股骨假体在全髋关节置换术后的临床效果
summary_zh.method: 回顾性分析大样本人群中两种假体的选择使用
summary_zh.result: 两种假体在特定选择下可获得相似临床结果

summary_en.motivation: To compare clinical outcomes of cemented versus uncemented femoral components in a broad population undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty for osteoarthritis.
summary_en.method: A retrospective analysis of selected use of the two implant types based on patient characteristics.
summary_en.result: Comparable clinical results can be achieved with both cemented and uncemented components when appropriately selected.
summary_en.validation: Clinical follow-up data from a large patient cohort.
